title: AWS database services and database migration
learningObjective: Choose between EC2-hosted and managed databases, identify relational (RDS, Aurora), NoSQL (DynamoDB) and in-memory (ElastiCache) databases, and identify migration tools (DMS, SCT).
foundation: You can run a database yourself on EC2 (full control, full work) or use a managed database where AWS handles setup, patching, backups and failover.
Relational databases (tables with SQL): Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora. NoSQL: Amazon DynamoDB. In-memory cache: Amazon ElastiCache.
AWS DMS moves databases to AWS with minimal downtime; AWS SCT converts schemas between different database engines.
engineer: EC2-hosted vs managed: choose EC2 for OS access, unsupported engines or specific configurations; choose managed (RDS/Aurora/DynamoDB) to offload patching, backups, Multi-AZ and scaling.

Amazon RDS: MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, Db2; automated backups, Multi-AZ, read replicas. Amazon Aurora: MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible, storage replicated six ways across three AZs, Aurora Serverless.

Amazon DynamoDB: serverless key-value/document NoSQL with single-digit millisecond performance, global tables, on-demand or provisioned capacity. Other purpose-built: DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible), Neptune (graph), Redshift (data warehouse), Keyspaces, Timestream.
Amazon ElastiCache (Valkey, Redis OSS, Memcached) and MemoryDB: in-memory caching and data stores to reduce latency and database load.

Migration: AWS DMS (homogeneous and heterogeneous migrations, continuous replication with change data capture); AWS SCT (schema and code conversion for heterogeneous migrations; DMS Schema Conversion offers similar capability in the console).

example.title: Modernising data
body: An Oracle database moves to Aurora PostgreSQL: SCT converts the schema and stored procedures, DMS replicates data with ongoing change capture until cutover. Session data moves to ElastiCache and the product catalog to DynamoDB.

prerequisites: An AWS account (use an IAM Identity Center user, not root)
permissions: Read-only access to explore; least-privilege permissions to change resources
limits: Conceptual objective: explore in the console; no configuration limits are tested

troubleshooting.symptom: Database CPU high from repeated reads.

troubleshooting.fix: Use EC2-hosted database (or RDS Custom where supported).

comparisons.difference: RDS ≈ Azure SQL Database/Azure Database for PostgreSQL/MySQL; DynamoDB ≈ Cosmos DB; ElastiCache ≈ Azure Cache for Redis; DMS ≈ Azure Database Migration Service.

misconceptions.myth: DMS converts schemas between engines by itself.
misconceptions.reality: SCT (or DMS Schema Conversion) converts schemas; DMS moves data.

architectureDecisions: Use purpose-built managed databases; reserve EC2-hosted databases for special requirements.

walkthrough.subtitle: Store orders, shopping carts and sessions, each in the right database, then migrate the old one.
learn: Managed databases vs a database on EC2

steps.label: Which DB?
steps.title: One app, three kinds of data
body: Orders need transactions and joins. Shopping carts need fast reads and writes at any scale. Login sessions need answers in microseconds.
One database type won't do all of these well.

steps.label: Managed vs EC2
steps.title: Run it yourself, or let AWS manage it?
body: You can install a database on an EC2 instance. Then you get full control of the OS and engine, but you handle patching, backups, scaling and failover.
Managed databases hand that work to AWS. Pick EC2 only when you need something a managed service doesn't allow.

steps.label: Relational
steps.title: Orders: relational with RDS or Aurora
body: Amazon RDS runs MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server and Db2 for you, with automated backups, patching and Multi-AZ failover.
Amazon Aurora is AWS's MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible engine, built for higher performance and availability.

steps.label: NoSQL
steps.title: Carts: NoSQL with DynamoDB
body: Amazon DynamoDB is a serverless key-value and document database. It returns results in single-digit milliseconds at any scale, with no servers to manage.
It suits simple, very high-volume access patterns, not complex joins.

steps.label: In-memory
steps.title: Sessions: in memory with ElastiCache
body: Amazon ElastiCache keeps data in memory (Valkey, Memcached or Redis OSS) and answers in microseconds. Use it as a cache in front of a database, or for sessions and leaderboards.
Amazon MemoryDB is the durable in-memory option.

callout.text: Relational = RDS / Aurora. NoSQL key-value = DynamoDB. In-memory cache = ElastiCache.

steps.label: Migrate
steps.title: Move the old database with DMS
body: AWS Database Migration Service copies data into AWS while the source database keeps running, then keeps it in sync with continuous replication until you switch over.
When the engine changes, for example Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL, the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (or DMS Schema Conversion) converts the schema and code.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: A database for each kind of data
body: Choose by the shape of the data and how it's accessed.
recap: Managed services take patching, backups and failover off you
RDS (six engines) and Aurora for relational
DMS migrates with ongoing replication; SCT converts schemas
